meta.source: Coded from the published QP and mark scheme (4MA1_1H_2311). Derived metadata only. No exam question text transcribed.

coding_notes: CROSSOVER BLOCK CONFIRMED: 1F q15-q24 = 1H q1-q10, ten questions worth 40 marks. Predicted from the matching mark sequence, confirmed by reading. Coded in the same sitting as IGCSE-NOV23-F-P1.

GAP-CANDIDATE differentiation — q16, 4 marks, the x coordinates of the two points on a cubic where the gradient takes a given value. Tagged solving_quadratic_equations_factorising as an INTERIM measure, consistent with Jun24 1H q18: once differentiated the work is solving x squared = k. FOURTH sighting, which takes this candidate to the minParts=4 bar.

GAP-CANDIDATE arithmetic_series_sum — q19, 6 marks. An arithmetic sequence is given by its first four terms, the sum of all terms is given, and the last term is wanted. Tagged simultaneous_equations and finding_the_nth_term as an INTERIM measure: both are genuinely demonstrated, since the route sets the nth-term rule against the sum formula and solves the pair. FOURTH sighting, also reaching the bar.

q22 is a tangent to a circle at a given point, and it does NOT need the equation of a circle: the route is that the tangent is perpendicular to the radius, then intercepts and Pythagoras. equation_of_a_circle stays excluded from the iGCSE courses on the evidence — this is the closest any coded paper has come to needing it, and it does not.
q14 tagged circle_theorem_angle_at_centre with angles_on_lines_and_circles for the isosceles triangle the two radii form. The 'give reasons' marks sit inside the same item.
q18 leads with cosine_rule rather than compound_units: a time is what is asked for, but the triangle work is where the marks are.
q24(b) tagged trig_graphs — reading the amplitude and vertical shift off a sketched cosine curve.
